question: Do two independent implementations of a static contact-angle wall condition on the SAME diffuse-interface free energy reproduce the prescribed (Young's law) angle on the same static-drop benchmark, and do they agree with each other?
reference: Young's law sigma_lg cos(theta) = sigma_sg - sigma_sl, evaluated with the wall free energy of the model under test: cos(theta) = (3 psi_w - psi_w^3)/2 with kappa = (3/4) sigma xi. Independent anchor -> the analytic law, not a simulation.

arms.dirichlet: wall VALUE psi_w (phase-field / Neumann-from-interface-thickness family, walberla PhaseFieldAllenCahn codegen ContactAngle, sailfish bc_wall_grad_phase)
arms.neumann_flux: wall FLUX kappa d_n psi = (3/4) sigma cos(theta) (1-psi^2) from the same wall free energy
arms.geometric_ghost: geometric ghost psi_ghost = psi_0 + cot(theta) |d_t psi|, no wall free energy (walberla free-surface ContactAngle.h / openLBMPM geometric family)

predeclared_rules: A row PASSES the anchor gate iff it is MEASURABLE and |theta_measured - theta_prescribed| / theta_prescribed <= accept_pct for BOTH independent estimators (theta_cap and theta_circle).

A row is MEASURABLE iff apex_height >= 2 xi AND circle_rms <= 0.15 xi AND both estimators are finite. Rows failing this are reported as NOT_MEASURABLE (a resolution limit of the measurement, not of the boundary condition) and are excluded from both the pass count and the median.

The XVAL of the two independent implementations PASSES iff (a) every measurable row of both arms passes the anchor gate, and (b) for every measurable angle |theta(neumann_flux) - theta(geometric_ghost)| / theta_prescribed <= cross_arm_pct.
No threshold may be relaxed after inspection; deviations are reported as honest FAIL with the failing rows enumerated.

numerics.descent: psi <- psi - omega (mu - <mu>), mu = a psi(psi^2-1) - kappa lap psi (mass-conserving Allen-Cahn descent, same fixed point as the Cahn-Hilliard no-flux steady state)
